title: Every warm edit-chat turn re-sends a ~46k-character digest of the whole cut list, and the conversation keeps every copy
what: A warm turn's CURRENT STATE still carries one line per known card with the first 60 characters of its words. At 500 cards that is 46,378 characters (104 KB), only 32% smaller than the full digest, and each copy stays in the provider conversation.
cost: About 35-45k fresh input tokens per chat message at 500 cards (estimated), plus about 400k tokens of history after ten turns, re-read every turn. The context window can be approached within a handful of turns on top of a ~322k-char corpus.
evidence: probe_digest.py: full 67,750 chars / 165,802 bytes, compact 46,378 chars / 104,286 bytes. _turn builds digest(engine, known) on every turn.
fix: Send known cards as [uid] person dur with no words, or only the cards changed since rev_seen plus a bare uid order. Keep highlights and the uid-rename resend property.

title: The 1.67 MB page goes out in full on every load: no validator, and the gzip is redone for each request
what: render_page caches the text, but _send gzips 1.67 MB on every request and sends no ETag or Cache-Control. The service worker's navigation arm is network-first and never caches it.
cost: About 35 ms of dashboard CPU and 557 KB on the wire per load, reload, pop-out window or phone open. A 304 is never possible.
evidence: Measured: doc 1,667,928 B; gzip level 5 32.7 ms giving 557,530 B; encode 1.07 ms; _sig 0.52 ms.
fix: Cache (bytes, gzip, etag=page_version()) per sig, and send ETag + Cache-Control: no-cache with a 304 on If-None-Match. Bytes are unchanged, so the golden test still holds.

title: Every pop-out panel window runs its own state poll loop
what: poll() starts unconditionally in every window, panel windows included, at 600 ms remote / 250 ms local. There is no visibility gating, and the BroadcastChannel carries only selection and playhead.
cost: Main window + 2 pop-outs + phone = about 6.7 requests/s per editor through the login gate, a2wsgi and engine.tick(), for as long as the windows are open.
evidence: Read: top-level poll() call, and PANEL never stops it.
fix: Panel windows take the main window's state over the channel, with a fallback poll; or slow polling while hidden. Keep the fast PENDING confirm.

title: Every Claude JSON turn leaves a temp directory and answer file that nothing deletes
what: Seven mkdtemp(prefix=timeline_cards_*) sites and no rmtree. _run_claude_json reads the answer and leaves the file.
cost: One directory per chat turn, search or describe, and about 50-60 per shortening pass, in container /tmp until the next recreate or in %TEMP% for good.
evidence: grep: mkdtemp in 7 places, rmtree in none.
fix: rmtree the answer's parent directory in a finally block in _run_claude_json, only when its name starts with timeline_cards_.

title: The transcript-search corpus re-walks the episode tree six times to answer one /api/search/scopes
what: corpus() re-lists every person and clip folder and stats every transcript on every call, and one scopes answer calls it 6 times.
cost: 15 people / 200 clips: 1,291 stats + 1,302 listdirs, 58 ms locally per modal open or scope change. Over SMB (standalone PC server) about 1-2.5 s (estimated), linear in clips.
fix: Memoise the signature for about 2 s, or pass one corpus through state/_expects. The hash semantics are unchanged.

title: A failed whisper corpus run leaves its scratch folder in %TEMP%
what: The scratch directory (run.json, .turns: MB of JSON) is removed only at the end of the success path, and run_worker raises when the worker fails.
cost: Each failed or retried transcribe on a GPU machine leaves MBs to tens of MBs that nothing prunes.

title: The two translation caches only ever grow, one entry per distinct text a cut has ever had
what: Keys are the exact cut text, so every trim, split or extend variant adds an entry that is never pruned. Every save is a whole-file read-merge-rewrite of a vault file shared by two processes.
cost: Estimated 0.5-5 MB per episode over a long edit. Each save and each cross-process refresh then parses the whole file (tens of ms).
fix: On save, drop old entries whose key is not a current card's key. Never drop the keys of live cards.
